case_number: Civil Appeal No 2016 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (C) No 4452 of 2022)
summary: The appeals challenge interim orders by the Delhi High Court concerning age eligibility criteria for the Delhi Judicial Service (DJS) and Delhi Higher Judicial Service (DHJS) examinations. The key issues include the validity of the upper age limit of 32 years for DJS and the reintroduction of a minimum age requirement of 35 years for DHJS. The appellant, High Court of Delhi, challenged the stay on examination schedules, arguing that delays were due to procedural issues and the pandemic. The respondents, including Devina Sharma, argued that strict application of amended age rules would unjustly exclude candidates who would have been eligible had exams been held on time. The Supreme Court considered equitable relief, especially for candidates aged out due to postponements, and examined constitutional validity under Article 233, which prescribes no minimum age for District Judges. The Court acknowledged the administrative burden but permitted late applications subject to final outcome.
legal_provisions_cited: Article 226 of the Constitution of India
Article 233 of the Constitution of India
Article 136 of the Constitution of India
Delhi Higher Judicial Service Rules, Rule 9(3)
final_judgment: Writ petitions transferred to the Supreme Court for final adjudication; respondents and intervenors permitted to submit applications subject to the final decision; matters listed for hearing on 14 March 2022.
